fragments.text: Over the past decade, the Indian regulatory framework has evolved significantly to accommodate emerging technologies while focusing on information accessibility. In this session, I will outline the policy initiatives and legislative reforms undertaken by the Indian government to regulate emerging technologies including AI while balancing public interest principles of access, autonomy, transparency and accountability. The Indian government acknowledges AI significance and a societal impact and various ministries are developing strategies for it. For instance, in 2015, the government launched the Digital India initiative with an emphasis on emerging technologies including AI. In 2018, the government's public policy think tank Nithi Ayo published the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence with the brand AI for all. The DPDP Act ensures transparency by introducing requirements of providing notice to a data principle, that is the individual to whom the data relates to, informing them about the personal data collected, the purpose of collection, and the manner of exercising the rights. The law also mandates providing access to the notice and requests for consent in English or any of the 22 languages listed in the Indian Constitution. The DPDP Act also ensures autonomy of data principles by empowering them to exercise rights such as the right to access information, the right to correct, complete, and erase personal data, the right to grievance, redress, and the right to nominate someone for exercising their rights in the event of death or incapacity.

Under the Information Technology Act, there are rules for online intermediaries, which in short are called the IT intermediary rules. These rules, amongst other things, prescribe due diligence obligations of an online intermediary like a social media platform or an e-commerce marketplace. From a transparency and accessibility perspective, these rules require an intermediary to prominently publish on their website, mobile application, or both the privacy policy and user agreement in English or any of the 22 languages specified in the Constitution.
